item.title: Ollama: Local LLM Inference for Personal Computers and Small Services
item.description:
Ollama packages model acquisition, local inference, a command-line interface, a desktop application, and an HTTP API into one tool. It is one of the easiest ways to download an open-weight model and run it on a developer workstation without first assembling a Python environment, inference engine, tokenizer, prompt template, and GPU runtime.

A minimal session is:

sh 
ollama pull qwen3:8b
ollama run qwen3:8b

Ollama selects an appropriate local runner, stores the model, starts it when needed, and applies the model’s chat template. This convenience makes Ollama a good fit for personal computers, application development, demonstrations, and small internal services. It does not automatically make a laptop into a high-throughput or highly available production inference cluster.

item.title: Docker-based Hadoop/Spark/Hive Orchestration
item.description:
Hadoop, Spark, and Hive have overlapping Java, Hadoop-client, and configuration requirements. Installing every distribution on a workstation also mixes cluster state with host files. A Docker Compose lab avoids both problems by mounting an immutable software tree at /opt/ro and placing daemon state in named volumes.

The guide builds the lab in five stages:

  1. Start an offline toolbox with the JDK, Hadoop, Hive, and Spark commands but no cluster daemons.
  2. Add one HDFS NameNode and three DataNodes.
  3. Add one YARN ResourceManager and three NodeManagers.
  4. Add HiveServer2 with an embedded Derby metastore.
  5. Run Spark locally and on YARN.

item.title: Fixing CVEs for Golang-based statically-linked Executables
item.description:
gosu is a container-friendly alternative to su/sudo written in go. It’s included in the base image one of our production image, which triggers https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-68121.

Generic Considerations for all Golang-based statically-linked Executables #

CVEs in a statically-linked golang program come from 2 sources:

  1. The software’s own code. This is just good old software CVEs
  2. golang standard SDK; official announcements. These CVEs exist in the toolchain used to build a specific executable.

Most times the Golang SDK is the one to blame, and fixing such CVEs is as simple as rebuild the program with latest golang SDK.

item.title: On Docker Image CVE Fixes and Prevention
item.description:
Rules of thumb:

  1. ensure your image have a proper security software-upgrade source configured - so apt-get upgrade (or the equivalent) doesn’t do nothing.
  2. Include RUN apt-get update && apt-get upgrade -y (or the equivalent) in your Dockerfile.
  3. In rare case involving statically-linked golang-based program, delete it or rebuild from source as part of your docker build.
  4. Schedule your own rebuild weekly or monthly.

Background #

  1. The single source of truth for Docker official images (DOI) is the master branch of https://github.com/docker-library/official-images. They use a format called “Library definition files” to define which tags in which repository should be actively rebuilt and where to find their Dockerfile (git repository URL and commit ID). These repo:tags are called currently maintained ones.
    • Most but not all of these referenced Dockerfile git repositories are maintained by Docker Inc. itself. For an example.
  2. A Jenkins job at https://doi-janky.infosiftr.net/ analyzes Dockerfiles of all DOIs, generates up-to-date dependencies among DOIs, and persists them to https://github.com/docker-library/meta.
  3. Using these metadata, every merged PR to a DOI Dockerfile triggers a rebuild and push to Docker Hub of all its downstream DOIs (those that FROM it) on https://doi-janky.infosiftr.net/.
    • Scheduled unconditional rebuilds are not guaranteed.

Observations #

  1. Docker Inc.’s DOIs do not RUN apt upgrade (or the equivalent) in the Dockerfile, nor are other DOI vendors required to do this.
  2. Even if a DOI vendor has the OS upgrade step in their Dockerfile, if there is no scheduled unconditional rebuild, security patches (if any) will not be installed.
  3. Some DOIs use a distro where security update upstream is disabled by default. See docker run --rm mysql:9.6.0 tail /etc/yum.repos.d/oracle-linux-ol9.repo for an example.

Consequently, currently maintained DOIs provide no guarantee of being CVE-free at the time of the build. Therefore, a no-op rebuild (without RUN apt upgrade or the equivalent) will not fix anything.

item.title: Docker-in-Docker
item.description:
Docker-in-Docker (DinD) runs a Docker daemon inside a container. It is sometimes useful for disposable CI jobs that must build or test images, but it adds privileged-kernel access, nested storage, and caching complexity. It is not the default choice for every job that invokes docker.

Choose the Right Build Model #

There are three common models:

  1. DinD: a dedicated daemon runs in the job network namespace. It provides separation from the host daemon but commonly needs privileged mode.
  2. Docker-outside-of-Docker: the job mounts the host Docker socket. It is simple and fast, but any process that can use the socket can control the host Docker daemon.
  3. Daemonless builders: BuildKit, Kaniko, Buildah, or a managed builder create OCI images without exposing a general-purpose host daemon.

Use the least privileged option that supports the build. Rootless BuildKit or a remote BuildKit builder can preserve cache efficiency without granting a CI job access to the runner’s Docker socket.

item.title: Browser Platform, Graphics, and Playwright in Docker
item.description:
Browser automation succeeds when tests model document loading, layout, networking, and rendering rather than treating a page as a static string.

Measure the Browser and DOM #

Browser dimensions answer different questions:

API Measurement
window.innerWidth and innerHeight Layout viewport, including a rendered scrollbar
window.outerWidth and outerHeight Browser window bounds
screen.width and screen.height Screen dimensions in CSS pixels
screen.availWidth and availHeight Screen space excluding reserved operating-system areas
element.clientWidth and clientHeight Content box plus padding, excluding border and scrollbar
element.scrollWidth and scrollHeight Scrollable content extent
element.offsetWidth and offsetHeight Border-box dimensions, rounded to integer pixels
element.getBoundingClientRect() Border-box geometry in viewport coordinates, retaining fractions

clientWidth is zero for an inline element without a layout box. On the root element, it describes the layout viewport without a classic scrollbar. Avoid mixing viewport coordinates from getBoundingClientRect() with document coordinates without adding the scroll offset.

item.title: Docker Fundamentals
item.description:
Docker, the container system that still depends on your kernel, your CPU ISA, and its x86-64 syscall. An application that runs in a docker container is said to be containerized.

Component Overview #

Docker Engine: dockerd #

dockerd is a CLI daemon program that manages installed containers on the local system. It is branded as Docker Engine or Docker CE (Community Edition), and is open-source and free.

The dockerd daemon listens on the UNIX domain socket /var/run/docker.sock for incoming clients. This socket file must be readable by the user who runs a docker client to establish the socket (to send HTTP request). If you installed the Docker Engine from your Linux distro’s package manager, this socket file may be only readable by the root or a special user group dedicated to Docker, e.g. docker. You may choose to add yourself to that user group, or simply become root whenever using the docker client. Use docker info to check if the dockerd is running and the client has permissions.
